profiles.assessment: The exact merged staging candidate passed the bounded Railway, Neon, R2, and Restate certification, but its execution runtime remains disabled by default or certification-only and shared deployment ports are not uniformly composed.

gap.disposition: Wire a production RuntimeTransport/activity implementation and concrete discovery/provider ports before claiming general Cloud execution readiness.

ports.runtimeTransport: DurableRemoteWorkflowRuntime over PostgreSQL RuntimeCommand and discovery repositories

profiles.assessment: The production entrypoint now composes attempt routing, immutable Managed Pi command translation, the PostgreSQL RuntimeCommand ledger, and durable outcome polling by default. The authenticated WebSocket server and Artifact-backed remote RuntimeNode terminal bridge still require supported production composition and server-profile certification.

gap.disposition: Compose the approved RuntimeNode identity source and Artifact-backed WebSocket bridge, then certify the Hosted Server restart matrix.

ports.runtimeTransport: Packaged ManagedPiProcessClient or injected DirectRuntimeActivityPort; unavailable acceptance otherwise

profiles.assessment: The all-in-one profile uses the shared Local core, rejects remote-gateway transport, and fails execution acceptance explicitly when no direct runtime is configured. Its packaged managed Pi RPC client resolves immutable SQLite inputs and completes through Local Restate; injected managed Pi and ACP direct execution plus SQLite restart recovery also pass.

gap.disposition: Certify the packaged managed Pi process client with a live provider and package a supported concrete ACP launcher.

compatibilityMatrix.assessment: Contracts, SDK, generated OpenAPI, and reachable NestJS controllers agree on all 11 versioned operations; the architecture drift test inspects the runtime controller graph.
Every workspace package version matches bun.lock and the corresponding release-please manifest entry; the manifest additionally owns the repository root version.
Drizzle checks enforce current PostgreSQL schema and migration snapshot agreement.
The current schema is deterministic and tested, but SQLite has no forward migration history beyond version 1.

gap.disposition: Add explicit forward migration and rollback/forward-repair evidence before schema version 2.

compatibilityMatrix.assessment: The compatibility check pins exact adapter, driver, transport, runtime, protocol, location, and profile combinations.
Declared internal imports resolve through package exports; no undeclared deep imports were found.
Core port packages point inward and do not import applications or concrete provider packages; adapter packages depend on the shared deployment port contracts as intended.
The repository-wide CODEOWNERS rule still names the placeholder @OWNER and therefore provides no actionable review authority.

gap.disposition: Replace the placeholder with the real owning user/team and verify protected-path review behavior.

compatibilityMatrix.assessment: The adapter has contract tests but no supported composition root consumes it; live cross-product certification remains deferred.

gap.disposition: Wire provider-neutral adapter selection into supported compositions or explicitly classify the adapter as library-only until M12.

compatibilityMatrix.assessment: Repository architecture reflects Restate/Railway/profile portability, while six canonical Drive sources remain unavailable and several retrieved sources retain superseded topology language.

gap.disposition: Reconcile canonical sources and preserve machine contract/schema ownership links.

persistenceParity.postgresql: Operator/Neon backup plus profile-portability export/import; no PersistenceProvider backup method
persistenceParity.sqlite: Online backup/restore with SHA-256 and quick_check
persistenceParity.assessment: SQLite has a concrete provider backup while PostgreSQL backup remains an external operational responsibility.

gap.disposition: Document and test the explicit PostgreSQL operator boundary with restore and forward-repair evidence.

persistenceParity.assessment: Both preserve immutable versions, lifecycle CAS, exact pins, and publish uniqueness.

persistenceParity.postgresql: PostgresCommandAcceptanceRepository with typed columns and CAS
persistenceParity.assessment: Both preserve duplicate replay, conflicting payload rejection, scope, retention input, and transition CAS.
Both retain immutable package identity and verify content digests on restore.

persistenceParity.postgresql: Typed execution and attempt tables with indexed lifecycle timestamps
persistenceParity.sqlite: SqliteExecutionRepository stores domain-validated JSON in revisioned records
persistenceParity.assessment: SQLite and PostgreSQL preserve the shared domain lifecycle, attempts, optimistic transitions, terminal references, and restart recovery; storage layouts differ intentionally by profile.
Both preserve immutable plan identity, schema version, and digest conflict detection.

persistenceParity.postgresql: 27 forward Drizzle migrations with schema drift check
persistenceParity.assessment: Clean creation works in both profiles, but rollback and future SQLite upgrade paths are not implemented as migration streams.

gap.disposition: Add versioned SQLite forward migrations and tested rollback/forward-repair procedures for both dialects.

persistenceParity.postgresql: Inbox, outbox, and execution-event tables with publication attempts
persistenceParity.sqlite: SqliteExecutionEventRepository with ordered append, publication CAS, pending query, archival, and reopen durability
persistenceParity.assessment: Both adapters persist ordered execution events and publication attempts; the SQLite adapter proves duplicate suppression and recovery after a full reopen.

persistenceParity.postgresql: Project state, revisions, mutations, and promotion proposal tables
persistenceParity.sqlite: Revisioned project state/history/mutation namespaces and StatePromotionProposal CAS repository
persistenceParity.assessment: Both adapters cover revision history, mutation replay, immutable proposal identity, concurrent review CAS, merge, reject, expire, and supersede transitions across restart or reopen.

persistenceParity.sqlite: SqliteReconciliationCheckpointRepository with observation-hash idempotency and version CAS
persistenceParity.assessment: Both adapters persist reconciliation decisions; SQLite duplicate observation and resolved-state recovery are proven after reopen.

persistenceParity.postgresql: Typed retention expiry, soft deletion, and publication attempt metadata
persistenceParity.sqlite: Retention values may exist inside JSON but no indexed expiry/deletion lifecycle
persistenceParity.assessment: SQLite cannot enforce or sweep accepted retention/deletion semantics at the persistence boundary.

gap.disposition: Add indexed expiry/deletion metadata and deterministic sweep/recovery tests.

persistenceParity.postgresql: Runtime command, delivery attempt, receipt, and inventory checkpoint repositories
persistenceParity.sqlite: Runtime command, event receipt/effect, and inventory checkpoint repositories with identity replay, CAS, atomic terminal transitions, and reopen durability
persistenceParity.assessment: Both adapters persist runtime commands, event receipts, and inventory checkpoints; SQLite proves duplicate, conflicting, out-of-order, and terminal replay across reopen.

lifecycleCoverage.assessment: Domain interactions and Restate waits are tested; profile reachability depends on real runtime wiring.
Execution lifecycle and workflow tests cover transitions, deadlines, and cancellation propagation.
Canonical payload hashes, replay, conflict, retention, and CAS are covered in PostgreSQL and SQLite command repositories.
Catalog, ContextPackage, ProjectState, policy, runtime, and ExecutionPlan references are digest/version pinned.
PostgreSQL and SQLite execution-event outboxes are durable; SQLite publication failure and pending replay survive a full reopen.
Restate submission uncertainty and remote command replay are covered; reconciliation checkpoints survive SQLite reopen with observation-hash idempotency.
Operational limits and PostgreSQL metadata are present; SQLite indexed retention/deletion is absent.
Domain transitions and compare-and-set semantics are tested for core PostgreSQL and SQLite repositories.
